raw.body:
## Summary

`flushComponentPerformance` reads `root._debugInfo` from the chunk. When
that array is empty and the chunk is fulfilled, it recovers the debug info
from the resolved value, but only when the value is an array, an async
iterable, a React element, or a lazy:

```js
if (debugInfo.length === 0 && root.status === 'fulfilled') {
  const resolvedValue = resolveLazy(root.value);
  if (
    typeof resolvedValue === 'object' && resolvedValue !== null &&
    (isArray(resolvedValue) ||
      typeof resolvedValue[ASYNC_ITERATOR] === 'function' ||
      resolvedValue.$$typeof === REACT_ELEMENT_TYPE ||
      resolvedValue.$$typeof === REACT_LAZY_TYPE) &&
    isArray(resolvedValue._debugInfo)
  ) {
    debugInfo = resolvedValue._debugInfo;
  }
}
```

A plain object root is excluded, so the Server Components track in the
Performance panel does not work for payloads whose root is a plain object,
even when the resolved value carries a `_debugInfo` array. Verified in
`react-server-dom-webpack@19.3.0-canary-28cd4bb0-20260723`.

## Context

Waku's RSC payload root is a plain object mapping slot ids to elements
(`Record<string, unknown>`), which lets one payload carry several named
elements. This shape is deliberate and we would like to keep it. Today we
patch the read site with a build transform that drops the type restriction,
which works but is coupled to the compiled output:

https://github.com/wakujs/waku/blob/main/packages/waku/src/lib/vite-plugins/patch-rsdw.ts

@vitejs/plugin-rsc documents the same shape constraint for its performance
track example (vitejs/vite-plugin-react#1152, vitejs/vite-plugin-react#1304).

## Request

Relax the recovery to accept any object value that carries an own
`_debugInfo` array. The type restriction seems to mirror
`moveDebugInfoFromChunkToInnerValue`, where it guards attaching
`_debugInfo` to the value. The read site only reads the property, so the
restriction does not appear to protect anything there, and the relaxation
is additive: values without `_debugInfo` behave as before.

If there is a supported way to get the performance track with a plain
object root without reshaping the payload, that guidance would also
resolve this for us.
raw.title: [Flight] Performance track debug info is not recovered for plain object roots
